title: User Interface
summary: Build Lightning Web Components that react, talk, call Apex and stay secure, and still handle Aura and Visualforce when the exam asks.

lessons.title: Reactivity: what makes LWC re-render
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, develop Lightning Web Components using reactive properties, decorators and template directives

cards.title: Every field is reactive
cards.body: Since Spring '20, **every class field** is reactive. If the template uses it and you **reassign** it, the component re-renders. No decorator needed for `count = 0; count++`.

cards.title: The 3 decorators
items: **@api**: public property or method, set by the parent or App Builder
**@track**: deep reactivity, so mutations *inside* an object or array re-render
**@wire**: data streamed in by a wire adapter

cards.title: Mutation vs reassignment
cards.body: For plain objects and arrays, either use @track or assign a new reference.

cards.title: No expressions in templates
cards.body: Templates allow only property references like `{fullName}`, not `{first + last}`. Put the logic in a **getter**: `get fullName() { return this.first + ' ' + this.last; }`. Getters re-run on every render.
**@api objects are read-only to the child.** Writing `this.record.Name = 'x'` in the child throws an error. Clone the object into a private field, or fire an event so the **owner** changes it.

Boolean @api property? **Default it to false** (or leave it unset). The presence of the attribute in markup means true. Use `lwc:if` / `lwc:elseif` / `lwc:else` for conditions and give every `for:each` item a `key`.

lessons.title: Lightning Data Service & the wire service
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, use Lightning Data Service, wire adapters and base record components to work with Salesforce data

cards.title: LDS = shared record cache
cards.body: **Lightning Data Service** reads and writes records through the UI API. It **caches** records and **shares** that cache, so every LDS component showing the record updates when one of them saves it. It also enforces **CRUD, FLS and sharing** for you.

cards.title: getRecord + getFieldValue
cards.body: '$recordId' makes the parameter reactive: when recordId changes, the wire fetches again.
In getRecord, **fields** returns an error if the user cannot see one of them. Put fields that some users may not see in **optionalFields** instead.

cards.title: Pick a base record component
items: **lightning-record-form**: fastest. Modes view, edit and readonly, but little layout control
**lightning-record-view-form** + lightning-output-field: read-only with a custom layout
**lightning-record-edit-form** + lightning-input-field: custom layout, plus onsubmit and onsuccess hooks

cards.title: Change values before saving
cards.body: Used with lightning-record-edit-form onsubmit={handleSubmit}.
Importing schema (`@salesforce/schema/...`) instead of using strings lets Salesforce **check that the field exists** and **block its deletion** while the component references it.

cards.title: Accessibility is free here
cards.body: Base components come with ARIA attributes, keyboard support and labels built in. Always set **label** (use variant="label-hidden" to hide it visually) and give icons **alternative-text**.

lessons.title: Calling Apex & keeping data fresh
lessons.objective: Given a set of requirements, develop Lightning Web Components that call Apex methods using wire or imperative calls

cards.title: Apex method checklist
items: **static**
**public** or **global**
**@AuraEnabled**
Import it: `import getX from '@salesforce/apex/MyCtrl.getX';`

cards.title: @wire needs cacheable=true
cards.body: To **@wire** an Apex method, annotate it `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`. Cacheable methods are **read-only**: any DML in them fails at runtime. To save data, call a non-cacheable method **imperatively** (it returns a Promise).

cards.title: Wire with refreshApex
cards.body: refreshApex takes the **provisioned value**, not just data.

cards.title: Apex changed an LDS record?
cards.body: LDS does not know what Apex did. After the Apex call resolves, call `notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([{ recordId }])` from **lightning/uiRecordApi**. LDS fetches the record again and updates every component that shows it. It replaces the older getRecordNotifyChange.
**"Wire reads, imperative writes."** Cache = wire. Clicks that save = imperative. Apex that saves and LDS on screen = notifyRecordUpdateAvailable.
Want to save without any Apex? Use **updateRecord** / **createRecord** / **deleteRecord** from lightning/uiRecordApi. They update the LDS cache automatically.

lessons.title: Lifecycle hooks & error handling
lessons.objective: Describe the Lightning Web Component lifecycle and implement error handling in components and their Apex controllers

cards.title: The lifecycle in order
items: **constructor()**: call super() first. Public properties are not set yet, so do not touch them
**connectedCallback()**: inserted into the DOM. Runs parent first, then child
**renderedCallback()**: after each render. Runs child first, then parent
**disconnectedCallback()**: removed from the DOM. Clean up here
**errorCallback(error, stack)**: catches errors from child components

cards.body: **renderedCallback runs after EVERY render.** Use a flag such as `if (this.chartReady) return;` for one-time work (third-party libraries), and do not change tracked state there, or the component re-renders in a loop.
**Connect and disconnect come in pairs.** Whatever you add in connectedCallback (window listeners, LMS subscriptions, intervals) you remove in disconnectedCallback.

cards.title: errorCallback = error boundary
cards.body: errorCallback catches errors thrown in the lifecycle hooks or rendering of **child** components. It does **not** catch the component's own errors. Put it in a parent wrapper and render a fallback UI.

cards.title: Friendly Apex errors
cards.body: In JS, read the message from `error.body.message`.

lessons.title: Talking between components
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, implement the correct method to communicate events through Lightning Web Components or Aura Components

cards.title: Pick the channel
items: Parent to child: **@api property** or **@api method**
Child to parent: **CustomEvent**
Unrelated components, even across LWC, Aura and Visualforce: **Lightning Message Service**

cards.title: Fire and handle
cards.body: Handler attribute = "on" + event name. Data travels in **detail**.
Event names: **no uppercase letters, no spaces**. Use underscores to separate words if you need to. Do not start the name with "on". `itemSelected` breaks, `itemselected` works.

cards.title: bubbles / composed (both default false)
items: false/false: only the child's host element receives it. Recommended
bubbles:true: bubbles up the DOM, but **stops at the shadow boundary**
bubbles + composed true: crosses every shadow boundary and leaks into everyone's DOM. Avoid it

cards.title: Lightning Message Service
cards.body: The channel is LightningMessageChannel metadata. Pass APPLICATION_SCOPE to receive messages from anywhere in the app.
**"Down = @api, Up = event, Sideways = LMS."**

lessons.title: Surfacing components: App Builder, Flow, actions & more
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, surface Lightning Web Components and Aura Components on Lightning pages, Visualforce pages, Quick Actions, Flows and Experience Cloud

cards.title: js-meta.xml
cards.body: Each **property** must match an **@api** field in the JS.

cards.title: Common targets
items: lightning__AppPage / RecordPage / HomePage
lightning__RecordAction (quick action)
lightning__FlowScreen
lightning__UtilityBar, lightning__Tab
lightningCommunity__Page + lightningCommunity__Default (Experience Builder)

cards.title: Quick actions
cards.body: Target **lightning__RecordAction**. With **actionType ScreenAction** the component opens in a modal. Close it with `CloseActionScreenEvent` from lightning/actions. With **actionType Action** the action is **headless**: no UI, and the platform calls your `@api invoke()` method.

cards.title: Flow screens
cards.body: To send a value back to the flow, dispatch `new FlowAttributeChangeEvent('prop', value)` from **lightning/flowSupport**. Add `@api validate()` that returns { isValid, errorMessage } to block the Next button.

cards.title: NavigationMixin
cards.body: Use NavigationMixin, never window.location. GenerateUrl returns a Promise.

cards.title: LWC inside Visualforce
cards.body: Use **Lightning Out**: add `<apex:includeLightning/>` and an Aura dependency app that `extends="ltng:outApp"`, then call `$Lightning.use(...)` and `$Lightning.createComponent(...)`.

**Dynamic Forms and Dynamic Actions** let admins place fields and actions on Lightning record pages with visibility rules, no code needed. Choose them over a custom component when the requirement is only "show this field when…".

lessons.title: Aura: still on the exam
lessons.objective: Given a set of requirements, select the appropriate Lightning Web Component, Aura Component, or Visualforce solution and describe its benefits

cards.title: Nesting rule
cards.body: An **Aura component can contain an LWC**. An **LWC cannot contain an Aura component**. To migrate, build the leaves in LWC first and keep Aura as the outer wrapper.

cards.title: Two Aura event types
items: **Component event**: goes up the containment hierarchy (capture, then bubble). Fire it with `cmp.getEvent('name')`
**Application event**: broadcast to every handler in the app. Fire it with `$A.get('e.c:MyEvt')`

cards.title: Component event
cards.code:
<!-- child.cmp -->
<aura:registerEvent name="selectEvt" type="c:SelectEvent"/>

<!-- parent.cmp -->
<aura:handler name="selectEvt" event="c:SelectEvent"
              action="{!c.handleSelect}"/>
cards.body: A component event handler needs **name** matching the registerEvent name.

cards.title: Application event
cards.body: In new builds, Lightning Message Service usually replaces application events.
Aura init: `<aura:handler name="init" value="{!this}" action="{!c.doInit}"/>`. Apex call: `cmp.get('c.method')`, setCallback, then `$A.enqueueAction(action)`.
**Name or no name?** `<aura:handler name="...">` handles component events. Leave the name out for application events. Swap them and the handler never fires.

lessons.title: Visualforce controllers & view state
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, use Visualforce standard controllers, custom controllers, extensions and StandardSetController

cards.title: Controller menu
items: **Standard controller**: standard actions and behavior, runs in **user mode**
**Extension**: adds to or overrides a standard or custom controller
**Custom controller**: all your own logic. Runs in **system mode**, so declare with sharing
**StandardSetController**: works on lists of records (list views, mass actions)

cards.title: Extension constructor
cards.body: For a set page, the constructor takes ApexPages.StandardSetController instead.
With `extensions="ExtA,ExtB"`, if two classes define the same method, the **leftmost** one (ExtA) wins.

cards.title: Mass action on list view
cards.body: In the extension, `ssc.getSelected()` returns the records checked in the list view.

cards.title: View state: 170 KB max
cards.body: Visualforce stores controller state in a hidden form field and sends it on every postback. Keep it small: mark values you do not need to keep as **transient**, query only the fields you need, and fetch read-only data with **JavaScript remoting**, which adds no view state.
**Transient = travel light.** Transient variables and static variables are **not** saved in view state.

lessons.title: Visualforce AJAX: partial refresh & async
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, use Visualforce to perform actions, partial page refreshes and asynchronous operations

cards.title: AJAX toolbox
items: **apex:actionSupport**: adds AJAX to a DOM event of a component (onchange)
**apex:actionFunction**: makes a JS function that calls a controller action
**apex:actionPoller**: calls an action on a timer
**apex:actionStatus**: shows a "loading…" indicator
**rerender="id1,id2"**: redraws only those components

cards.body: You **cannot rerender** a component that was not rendered (rendered="false") when the page loaded. Wrap it in an always-rendered **apex:outputPanel** and rerender the wrapper.

cards.title: actionFunction
cards.code:
<apex:actionFunction name="recalc" action="{!recalculate}"
                     rerender="totals">
  <apex:param name="qty" assignTo="{!qty}" value=""/>
</apex:actionFunction>
<!-- JS: recalc(5); -->
cards.body: Posts the view state, runs the action, then rerenders.

cards.title: JavaScript remoting
cards.body: Remote actions are **static**, send **no view state**, and return the result to a JS callback.
**actionFunction = "Visualforce does the redraw." Remoting = "JS does everything, fast and stateless."**

lessons.title: UI security: XSS, CSP, LWS & FLS
lessons.objective: Identify and prevent security vulnerabilities in Visualforce and Lightning components and enforce data access in their Apex controllers

cards.title: XSS in Visualforce
cards.body: Merge fields are **HTML-escaped by default**. `escape="false"` on apex:outputText turns escaping off, so user input can run as script. Do not use it with user-controlled data.

cards.title: Encode for the context
items: Inside <script>: **JSENCODE()**
JS inside an HTML attribute (onclick): **JSINHTMLENCODE()**
Raw HTML output: **HTMLENCODE()**
In a URL: **URLENCODE()**

cards.title: CSP in Lightning
cards.body: Lightning pages enforce **Content Security Policy**. Inline `<script>` tags and CDN scripts are blocked. Upload libraries as a **static resource** and load them with `loadScript` / `loadStyle` from **lightning/platformResourceLoader**. To fetch() an external API from the browser, add the domain as a **Trusted URL** (formerly CSP Trusted Sites).

cards.title: Lightning Web Security
cards.body: **LWS** is the newer replacement for **Lightning Locker**. It isolates each namespace in a JavaScript sandbox and changes risky APIs ("distortions"). Components can still import modules from other namespaces, which Locker blocked.

**LDS and base record components enforce CRUD and FLS. Your @AuraEnabled Apex does NOT, unless you make it.** Use `WITH USER_MODE` in SOQL, `Security.stripInaccessible()`, or `AccessLevel.USER_MODE` for DML. The sharing keywords control **record access only**.
In LWC, never write user data to `innerHTML` (for example inside an lwc:dom="manual" container). Use `lightning-formatted-rich-text`, which sanitizes its content.

flashcards.front: Is a plain class field reactive in LWC?
flashcards.back: Yes. Reassigning any field used in the template re-renders it. Mutating properties inside an object or array needs @track or a new reference.

flashcards.front: When do you still need @track?
flashcards.back: To re-render when you mutate a property inside a plain object or an element of an array without reassigning the field.

flashcards.front: What does @api do?
flashcards.back: Makes a property or method public: settable by the owner component, App Builder or Flow, or callable from a parent through querySelector.

flashcards.front: Can a child change an @api object it received?
flashcards.back: No. It is read-only. Clone it into a private field, or dispatch an event so the owner updates it.

flashcards.front: What makes a wire parameter reactive?
flashcards.back: A '$' prefix in a string, e.g. { recordId: '$recordId' }. The wire fetches again when that property changes.

flashcards.front: getRecord: fields vs optionalFields?
flashcards.back: fields returns an error if the user cannot access one of them. optionalFields leaves inaccessible fields out without an error.

flashcards.front: Which uiRecordApi helper reads a value from a record?
flashcards.back: getFieldValue(record, FIELD), using a field imported from @salesforce/schema. getFieldDisplayValue returns the formatted value.

flashcards.front: What does getPicklistValues need?
flashcards.back: A recordTypeId (often defaultRecordTypeId from getObjectInfo) and the fieldApiName.

flashcards.front: What are the rules for wiring an Apex method?
flashcards.back: Static, public or global, @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true). Cacheable methods cannot perform DML.

flashcards.front: What do you pass to refreshApex?
flashcards.back: The whole value the wire provisioned (the result object), not result.data. It returns a Promise.

flashcards.front: Apex updated a record shown by LDS. What do you call?
flashcards.back: notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([{ recordId }]) from lightning/uiRecordApi. It replaces getRecordNotifyChange.

flashcards.front: How do you send a friendly error message from Apex to LWC?
flashcards.back: Throw new AuraHandledException(message). The client reads it from error.body.message.

flashcards.front: In what order do connectedCallback and renderedCallback run for parent and child?
flashcards.back: connectedCallback runs parent first, then child. renderedCallback runs child first, then parent.

flashcards.front: What does errorCallback catch?
flashcards.back: Errors from child (descendant) components in their lifecycle hooks or rendering, not errors from the component itself. It is an error boundary.

flashcards.front: What are the CustomEvent defaults?
flashcards.back: bubbles: false, composed: false. Only the host element of the firing component receives the event.

flashcards.front: What are the naming rules for LWC events?
flashcards.back: No uppercase letters and no spaces. Use underscores if needed. Do not prefix the name with "on". The handler is on + eventname.

flashcards.front: When should you use Lightning Message Service?
flashcards.back: To communicate between components that are not related, across the DOM, including between LWC, Aura and Visualforce on the same Lightning page.

flashcards.front: What is the LMS scope that reaches the whole app?
flashcards.back: APPLICATION_SCOPE, passed in the subscribe options. By default, a subscriber only receives messages while it is in the active area.

flashcards.front: Which target exposes an LWC as a quick action?
flashcards.back: lightning__RecordAction, with actionType ScreenAction (modal) or Action (headless, using @api invoke()).

flashcards.front: How does a Flow screen LWC send a value back to the flow?
flashcards.back: Dispatch new FlowAttributeChangeEvent('propName', value) from lightning/flowSupport. The property must be @api and declared in the targetConfig.

flashcards.front: Which targets put an LWC in Experience Builder?
flashcards.back: lightningCommunity__Page (available in the builder) and lightningCommunity__Default (editable properties).

flashcards.front: How do you show an LWC on a Visualforce page?
flashcards.back: Lightning Out: <apex:includeLightning/>, an Aura app that extends ltng:outApp, then $Lightning.use() and $Lightning.createComponent().

flashcards.front: Can an LWC contain an Aura component?
flashcards.back: No. Aura can contain LWC, but LWC cannot contain Aura.

flashcards.front: How is an Aura component event handled, compared with an application event?
flashcards.back: Component event: aura:handler with name matching registerEvent. Fired with cmp.getEvent(). Application event: aura:handler with no name. Fired with $A.get("e.c:Evt").

flashcards.front: What is the Visualforce view state limit?
flashcards.back: 170 KB. Reduce view state with transient variables, smaller queries and JavaScript remoting.

flashcards.front: Two extensions define save(). Which one runs?
flashcards.back: The leftmost one in the extensions attribute.

flashcards.front: What is the StandardSetController constructor parameter for an extension?
flashcards.back: ApexPages.StandardSetController. The page uses standardController plus recordSetVar.

flashcards.front: actionFunction vs JavaScript remoting?
flashcards.back: actionFunction posts the view state and can rerender parts of the page. Remoting calls a static @RemoteAction with no view state and returns the result to a JS callback.

flashcards.front: How do you use a merge field safely inside a <script> block?
flashcards.back: Wrap it in JSENCODE(), e.g. var n = '{!JSENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.n)}';

flashcards.front: How do you load a third-party JS library in LWC?
flashcards.back: Upload it as a static resource and call loadScript(this, resourceUrl) from lightning/platformResourceLoader. CDN script tags are blocked by CSP.

flashcards.front: Does @track see changes inside a Set, Map or Date?
flashcards.back: No. LWC observes plain objects and arrays only. For Set, Map, Date or class instances, assign a new object to rerender.

flashcards.front: StandardSetController record limit
flashcards.back: 10,000 records. A query locator returning more throws a LimitException; a List with more is truncated.

flashcards.front: Stop updateRecord from overwriting someone else's save
flashcards.back: Pass clientOptions { ifUnmodifiedSince: lastModifiedDate } (LastModifiedDate read through a wire adapter).

questions.q: A component shows {count} in its template. The class declares count = 0; with no decorator, and a button handler runs this.count++. What happens when the button is clicked?
options: It re-renders and shows the new value, since reassigned fields are reactive
Nothing changes on screen until count is decorated with @track, because primitive fields are not observed
Nothing changes on screen until count is decorated with @api
The template only updates if count is exposed through a getter
questions.explain: All LWC class fields are reactive. When a field used in the template gets a new value (this.count++ is a reassignment), the component re-renders.
wrong: @track is only needed to observe changes inside an object or array, not for primitives.
@api makes a property public. It is not needed for reactivity.
A getter is not needed. The field itself is reactive.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Reactivity

questions.q: A developer clicks the button that calls handleClose(), but the template that shows {filters.status} still says "Open". Which two changes would make the UI update? (Choose 2)
options: Decorate filters with @api
Call this.render() at the end of handleClose()
Decorate filters with @track
Assign a new object: this.filters = { ...this.filters, status: 'Closed' };
Move the assignment into renderedCallback()
questions.explain: Without @track, LWC only notices when the field itself gets a new value, not when a property inside the object changes. @track adds deep observation, and a new object reference is a reassignment.
wrong: @api makes the field public. It does not add deep reactivity, and a component should not change its own public properties.
There is no supported render() call that forces a re-render.
Changing state in renderedCallback can cause a render loop, and it is still a mutation that LWC does not observe.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Reactivity for Fields, Objects, and Arrays

questions.q: A component must show a contact's full name built from its firstName and lastName fields. What is the correct way to show it in the template?
options: Use {firstName + ' ' + lastName} directly in the template, like an Aura expression
Set a fullName field inside renderedCallback()
Define get fullName() in the class and reference {fullName}
Use an @wire decorator to combine the two fields
questions.explain: LWC templates do not allow expressions. Computed values belong in a getter, which is evaluated again on each render.
wrong: Expressions are not allowed in LWC templates and cause a compile error.
Setting state in renderedCallback triggers another render, which risks an infinite loop.
@wire provisions data from wire adapters. It does not compute local values.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Getters to Compute a Value

questions.q: A parent passes an Account object to a child through <c-acct-editor record={acct}>. The child declares @api record and runs this.record.Name = this.newName when the user types, which throws an error. What should the developer do?
options: Decorate record with @track in addition to @api so the child gets its own writable, deep-tracked copy
Move the assignment into the child's constructor
Use JSON.stringify(this.record) before assigning
Copy the object into a private field and edit the copy, or fire an event so the parent updates acct
questions.explain: Objects passed to @api properties are read-only to the child, because the owner owns the data. The child either works on a copy or tells the owner about the change with an event (data down, events up).
wrong: A field cannot use both @api and @track. Doing so does not make the parent's object writable.
Public properties are not set yet in the constructor, and the object is still read-only.
Turning the object into a string does not let the child change the original property.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Public Properties / Data Flow

questions.q: On an Account record page, a component must show Name, Industry and Phone as read-only values and respect each user's field-level security. The requirement is the least code possible. What should the developer use?
options: An @AuraEnabled Apex method that queries Name, Industry and Phone, shown in a custom HTML template
lightning-record-form with object-api-name, record-id, fields and mode="readonly"
A Visualforce page embedded in an iframe
getRecord with a custom template of lightning-formatted-text elements
questions.explain: lightning-record-form is the fastest way to show a record. It uses Lightning Data Service, so it enforces CRUD, FLS and sharing without Apex.
wrong: This needs more code, and Apex does not enforce FLS unless you code it.
This adds complexity and does not fit Lightning Experience well.
This works, but it needs more code than one base component.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compare Base Components (lightning-record-form)

questions.q: A component calls getRecord with fields: [NAME_FIELD, RATING_FIELD]. Users without field-level access to Account.Rating see an error, and the Name is not shown either. What is the best fix?
options: Mark the Apex controller as without sharing
Use layoutTypes: ['Full'] instead of fields
Move RATING_FIELD into optionalFields
Wrap the @wire decorator in a try/catch block
questions.explain: With fields, getRecord returns an error if any listed field is inaccessible. With optionalFields, inaccessible fields are simply left out of the response.
wrong: getRecord uses LDS, not Apex, and sharing does not control field-level security.
This changes which fields are returned and does not deal with optional access in a predictable way.
Wire errors arrive in the provisioned error property. They are not thrown, so try/catch cannot catch them.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: getRecord

questions.q: A developer needs a two-column custom form to create Case records. Before saving, the component must set Origin to "Web" without showing that field to the user. Which approach meets this?
options: lightning-record-form with mode="edit" and an onsuccess handler that sets Origin
lightning-record-view-form with a lightning-output-field for each field, plus a hidden lightning-output-field for Origin set to Web
A getRecord wire adapter with a lightning-input for each field
lightning-record-edit-form with onsubmit: call preventDefault(), add Origin to event.detail.fields, then submit(fields)
questions.explain: lightning-record-edit-form allows a custom layout, and its submit event lets you change the field values before calling submit(fields).
wrong: onsuccess fires after the save, which is too late, and record-form gives little control over the layout.
The view form is read-only. It cannot create records, and output fields cannot set values.
getRecord only reads data. Saving would still need createRecord and hand-built field handling.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Override Default Behaviors (lightning-record-edit-form)

questions.q: A team is choosing between Lightning Data Service and custom Apex for a set of record components. Which two statements about Lightning Data Service are true? (Choose 2)
options: It refreshes its cache automatically when an Apex method updates the same record
Records are cached and shared, so when one LDS component saves a record, other LDS components that show it update
It enforces CRUD, field-level security and sharing for the running user
It needs an @AuraEnabled Apex method to read field values
updateRecord can update thousands of records in one bulk call
questions.explain: LDS keeps a shared client cache that keeps components in sync, and it runs with the user's permissions.
wrong: LDS does not know about Apex DML. You must call notifyRecordUpdateAvailable.
LDS reads records through the UI API without Apex.
updateRecord works on one record per call. Large bulk changes belong in Apex.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lightning Data Service

questions.q: A developer adds @wire(getOpenCases) to an LWC. The Apex method is public static and annotated @AuraEnabled, but the component fails to load the data. What change is needed?
options: Make the method global
Change the annotation to @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)
Add the @RemoteAction annotation
Decorate the property with @track
questions.explain: Only Apex methods marked @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) can be wired. Non-cacheable methods must be called imperatively.
wrong: public is enough for an @AuraEnabled method.
@RemoteAction is for Visualforce JavaScript remoting.
@track has no effect on whether Apex can be wired.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) method creates a Task record and returns the new Id. The LWC calls it imperatively when a button is clicked. What is the result, and what is the fix?
options: It fails at runtime: cacheable methods cannot do DML. Remove cacheable=true and keep the imperative call
It works, but later clicks return the cached Id instead of creating a Task. Add @track to the result to avoid stale values
It fails because imperative calls must use @wire. Switch to @wire
It works only when the class is declared without sharing
questions.explain: Cacheable methods must not change data, and DML inside them fails. A method that saves data should not be cacheable, and it is called imperatively.
wrong: The DML itself fails, and @track does not control the cache.
Imperative calls are the right way to call non-cacheable methods.
Sharing does not lift the DML restriction on cacheable methods.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Call Apex Methods Imperatively

questions.q: After saveContact() succeeds, the contact list does not refresh, and refreshApex does nothing. What should the developer change?
options: Mark saveContact as cacheable=true so it shares the wire cache with getContacts and refreshes it on save
Call getContacts imperatively inside renderedCallback()
Decorate contacts with @track so refreshApex can see changes
Keep the whole provisioned result (this.wiredResult = result) and pass that to refreshApex
questions.explain: refreshApex needs the exact value the wire service provisioned (the object that holds data and error). Passing only the data array does not refresh anything.
wrong: A method that performs DML cannot be cacheable.
This calls Apex again on every render and is wasteful.
Reactivity is not the problem. refreshApex received the wrong value.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Refresh the Cache When Using @wire

questions.q: An LWC calls an imperative Apex method that updates the Account's Rating. A lightning-record-form on the same record page still shows the old Rating. Which two approaches are recommended? (Choose 2)
options: After the Apex promise resolves, call notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([{ recordId: this.recordId }])
Mark the Apex method cacheable=true
Use updateRecord from lightning/uiRecordApi instead of Apex for this single-record update
Call refreshApex(this.recordId)
Reload the page with window.location.reload() after the Apex promise resolves to show the new Rating
questions.explain: LDS does not see Apex DML, so you tell it with notifyRecordUpdateAvailable. Saving through LDS (updateRecord) updates the shared cache directly.
wrong: Cacheable methods cannot perform DML.
refreshApex refreshes a wired Apex result, not an LDS record, and recordId is not a provisioned value.
A full reload is bad UX and is not the supported pattern.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: notifyRecordUpdateAvailable

questions.q: A component adds a window resize listener. Users report memory leaks after moving between pages. Where should the listener be added and removed?
options: Add it in the constructor and remove it in renderedCallback()
Add it in renderedCallback() and never remove it
Add it in connectedCallback() and remove it in disconnectedCallback()
Add it in errorCallback() and remove it in connectedCallback()
questions.explain: connectedCallback runs when the component is inserted and disconnectedCallback when it is removed, so they are the matching place to set up and clean up global listeners.
wrong: renderedCallback runs after every render, so the listener would be removed at the wrong times.
This adds a new listener on each render and leaks them.
errorCallback handles errors from child components. It is not for setup.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lifecycle Hooks

questions.q: A developer loads a charting library with loadScript and draws a chart into a <div lwc:dom="manual"> inside renderedCallback(). The chart is drawn again every time any property changes. What is the best fix?
options: Move the code into the constructor, which runs once per component instance, before any property changes
Add a boolean guard such as chartInitialized so the setup only runs once
Call loadScript from disconnectedCallback()
Decorate the chart field with @api
questions.explain: renderedCallback runs after every render. One-time work such as loading and setting up a library needs a guard flag.
wrong: In the constructor, the template has not rendered yet, so the div does not exist.
disconnectedCallback runs when the component is removed.
@api has no effect on how often renderedCallback runs.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Third-Party JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: When a DML error occurs in an @AuraEnabled method, users see a generic "Script-thrown exception" message. The business wants a clear, custom message in the LWC toast. What should the developer do?
options: In Apex, catch it and throw new AuraHandledException('clear message'); in JS, read error.body.message
Return null from the method and check for null in JS
Use System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, message) so the message shows in the browser console and the toast
Wrap the imperative call in errorCallback()
questions.explain: AuraHandledException sends a custom message to the client in error.body.message, instead of a generic exception message.
wrong: Returning null hides the error and gives the user no information.
System.debug writes to debug logs, not to the browser.
errorCallback is a lifecycle hook that catches errors from child components. It does not receive Apex errors from a promise.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors / Apex Developer Guide: AuraHandledException

questions.q: A dashboard holds six child LWCs. If any child throws an error while rendering, the dashboard must show a friendly fallback panel and log the stack. Where should the developer put this logic?
options: A try/catch block in each child's connectedCallback()
errorCallback() in each child component
A window.onerror handler in the dashboard's renderedCallback() that swaps in the fallback panel and logs the stack
errorCallback(error, stack) in the parent dashboard, which sets a flag to render the fallback
questions.explain: errorCallback acts as an error boundary. It catches errors from descendant components, but not errors from the component itself, so it belongs in the parent.
wrong: This does not catch rendering errors, and it repeats the same code in every child.
A component's errorCallback does not catch its own errors.
Global handlers do not fit the LWC model and run into security restrictions.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: errorCallback()

questions.q: A child component shows a list of products. When the user clicks one, its parent must receive the product Id. What should the developer do?
options: Publish the Id on a Lightning Message Service channel that the parent subscribes to in connectedCallback()
Dispatch a CustomEvent with the Id in detail, and listen with an on<eventname> attribute in the parent
Set an @api property on the parent from the child
Store the Id in sessionStorage and poll it from the parent
questions.explain: Child-to-parent communication uses a CustomEvent. The data goes in detail, and the parent listens declaratively in its template.
wrong: LMS is for components that are not related. It is too heavy for a parent and child.
A child cannot set its parent's public properties. Data flows down only.
Polling storage is a fragile anti-pattern.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Communicate with Events

questions.q: A child runs this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('itemSelected')). The parent markup is <c-item onitemSelected={handle}></c-item>, but handle never runs. What is the fix?
options: Set bubbles: true on the event
Set composed: true on the event
Rename the event to itemselected and use onitemselected in the parent markup
Add a handler in the parent with this.template.addEventListener('itemSelected')
questions.explain: LWC event names should have no uppercase letters, because HTML attribute names are not case-sensitive. A lowercase event name with a matching on handler works.
wrong: The parent listens on the child's host element, so bubbling is not needed.
Crossing shadow boundaries is not the issue.
The naming problem is still there, and the template listens on the wrong node.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Create and Dispatch Events

questions.q: A Lightning app page holds a Visualforce page, an Aura component and an LWC in separate regions. When a record is selected in the LWC, the other two must react. What should the developer use?
options: Lightning Message Service with a custom message channel
A CustomEvent with bubbles: true and composed: true
An Aura application event fired from the LWC
An @api method on the Visualforce page
questions.explain: LMS is the supported way to communicate across the DOM between Visualforce, Aura and LWC on the same Lightning page.
wrong: DOM events cannot reach a Visualforce iframe or components that are not related.
An LWC cannot fire Aura application events directly.
A Visualforce page cannot expose @api methods.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Communicate Across the DOM with Lightning Message Service

questions.q: c-grandparent's template contains <c-child onnotify={handleNotify}>. c-child's template contains <c-grandchild>, which dispatches the event below. handleNotify never runs. Why, and what is the recommended fix?
questions.code:
// grandchild.js
this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('notify', { bubbles: true }));
options: The event name is invalid. Rename it to onNotify
composed is false, so the event stops at c-child's shadow boundary; c-child should re-fire its own event
bubbles must be false for parents to listen
The grandparent must call this.template.addEventListener('notify', ...) in its constructor to catch deeper events
questions.explain: With bubbles: true and composed: false, the event does not cross c-child's shadow boundary. Re-dispatching keeps each component's events part of its own API. composed: true would also work, but it is discouraged because the event leaks everywhere.
wrong: Event names must not start with "on", and should not contain uppercase letters.
Bubbling is not what stops the event. The shadow boundary is.
In the constructor the child elements do not exist yet, and the boundary would still block the event.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure Event Propagation

questions.q: An LWC must be available in Lightning App Builder only on Account record pages. What is the correct configuration in its js-meta.xml?
options: isExposed true, target lightning__AppPage
isExposed false, target lightning__RecordPage, and a targetConfig for lightning__RecordPage listing <object>Account</object>
isExposed true, target lightning__RecordPage, and a targetConfig for it with <object>Account</object>
isExposed true, target lightningCommunity__Page with objects Account
questions.explain: isExposed makes the component available in builders. The record page target plus the objects list limits where it can be placed.
wrong: An App Page is not a record page.
With isExposed false, the component does not appear in App Builder at all.
This target is for Experience Builder pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: XML Configuration File Elements

questions.q: Admins must be able to set a component's heading text and maximum row count in Lightning App Builder. Which two steps are required? (Choose 2)
options: Declare @api heading and @api maxRows in the JS class
Create a .design file for the LWC
Add <property> elements for heading and maxRows in a targetConfig in js-meta.xml
Decorate the fields with @track
Store heading and maxRows in a custom metadata type that App Builder reads at design time
questions.explain: App Builder properties are declared as <property> elements in js-meta.xml, and each one must match a public @api property in the class.
wrong: .design files are used for Aura components, not LWC.
@track does not make a property public.
Custom metadata does not create App Builder properties.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure a Component for Lightning App Builder

questions.q: A button in an LWC must open the standard "New Contact" form. The solution must work in Lightning Experience and the Salesforce mobile app. What should the developer do?
options: Set window.location to '/003/e'
Use an <a href="/lightning/o/Contact/new"> link, the Lightning Experience URL that opens the standard New Contact form
Dispatch a CustomEvent named navigate
Use NavigationMixin and this[NavigationMixin.Navigate] with type standard__objectPage, Contact and actionName new
questions.explain: NavigationMixin uses page references, so navigation works the same way across Lightning Experience, mobile and Experience Cloud.
wrong: A hard-coded Classic URL breaks in containers and mobile.
A hard-coded URL is fragile and skips the navigation service.
A custom event does not navigate anywhere.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Navigate to Pages, Records, and Lists

questions.q: A custom LWC on a Flow screen lets the user pick a warehouse. The flow must use the picked warehouse Id in later elements. Which two steps are required? (Choose 2)
options: Publish the Id on a Lightning Message Service channel, and read it in later flow elements as a screen output
Declare an @api warehouseId property and list it as a <property> in the lightning__FlowScreen targetConfig
Dispatch FlowNavigationFinishEvent with the Id
Return the Id from connectedCallback()
Dispatch FlowAttributeChangeEvent('warehouseId', id) from lightning/flowSupport when a warehouse is picked
questions.explain: Flow reads outputs from properties declared for the flow screen target. FlowAttributeChangeEvent tells the flow runtime that the value changed.
wrong: Flow does not read LMS messages as screen outputs.
This event ends the flow. It does not set output values.
Return values from lifecycle hooks are ignored.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure a Component for Flow Screens

questions.q: In an Aura app, a child component must notify only the component that contains it when a row is selected. Which mechanism fits best?
options: A component event registered with aura:registerEvent and fired with cmp.getEvent()
An application event fired with $A.get()
Lightning Message Service with APPLICATION_SCOPE, using lightning:messageChannel in the parent
A platform event
questions.explain: Component events travel up the containment hierarchy, so they are the right fit for a child notifying its container.
wrong: Application events go to every handler in the app, which is too broad.
LMS is for communication across the DOM between components that are not related.
Platform events are server-side messaging, not UI messaging.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Component Events

questions.q: An Aura component must broadcast that a record changed to any component in the app that has a handler for c:RecordChanged. Which client-side code fires it correctly?
options: var e = cmp.getEvent('RecordChanged'); e.fire();
var e = $A.get('e.c:RecordChanged'); e.setParams({ recordId: id }); e.fire();
this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('recordchanged'));
$A.enqueueAction('e.c:RecordChanged');
questions.explain: Application events are obtained with $A.get('e.namespace:eventName'), given parameters with setParams, and fired with fire().
wrong: cmp.getEvent fires a component event that was registered with that name.
This is LWC syntax for DOM events.
enqueueAction queues server actions, not events.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Fire Application Events

questions.q: A team has a large Aura component and wants to rebuild one of its sections as a new LWC without rewriting the whole thing. What is the supported approach?
options: Put the Aura component inside the new LWC's template
It is not possible. The whole Aura component must be rewritten
Embed the new LWC inside the existing Aura component's markup
Load the Aura component in the LWC with loadScript
questions.explain: Aura components can contain LWCs, but LWCs cannot contain Aura components. Migrate from the inside out.
wrong: An LWC cannot contain an Aura component.
Aura and LWC can work together, so step-by-step migration is supported.
loadScript loads JS libraries from static resources, not components.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Migrate Aura Components / Compose Aura Components from LWC

questions.q: The child fires its component event, but the parent's handleSelect never runs. What is wrong?
questions.code:
<!-- child.cmp -->
<aura:registerEvent name="selectEvt" type="c:SelectEvent"/>
<!-- childController.js -->
var evt = cmp.getEvent("selectEvt");
evt.setParams({ rowId: id });
evt.fire();

<!-- parent.cmp -->
<aura:handler event="c:SelectEvent" action="{!c.handleSelect}"/>
<c:child/>
options: The child must use $A.get('e.c:selectEvt') to fire the event, since cmp.getEvent() only reaches the child
setParams must be called after fire()
The parent must register the event as well
The aura:handler lacks name="selectEvt", so it only handles application events
questions.explain: A component event handler must include a name that matches the aura:registerEvent name. Without it, the handler is treated as an application event handler.
wrong: $A.get is used for application events. The child correctly fires a component event.
Parameters must be set before the event is fired.
Only the component that fires the event registers it.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Handling Component Events

questions.q: A Visualforce page for Opportunity must keep the standard Save and Cancel behavior and add one custom "Calculate Discount" action. What is the most efficient approach?
options: A custom controller that rebuilds save() and cancel() with DML and PageReference logic
A StandardSetController
The Opportunity standard controller plus an extension that adds the method
A JavaScript remoting class only
questions.explain: An extension adds behavior to a standard controller and keeps the standard actions for free.
wrong: Rebuilding the standard actions is wasted effort.
StandardSetController is for lists of records.
Remoting does not give you the standard actions.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Building a Controller Extension

questions.q: Sales managers want to select several Accounts in a list view and click a button that sets Rating to "Hot" on the selected records. How should the Visualforce page be built?
options: standardController plus recordSetVar, and an extension that takes StandardSetController and uses getSelected()
standardController="Account" and an extension that takes ApexPages.StandardController and calls getRecord() on it
A custom controller that queries every Account
An apex:actionPoller that updates the records
questions.explain: Setting recordSetVar makes the page a list page. The StandardSetController then returns the records the user selected in the list view through getSelected().
wrong: StandardController works on one record and cannot see the list view selection.
Querying every Account ignores the user's selection.
A poller runs actions on a timer and has no access to the selection.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Standard List Controllers / StandardSetController

questions.q: A Visualforce page fails with "Maximum view state size limit exceeded". The controller holds a large list that is used only to draw a read-only table. Which two changes reduce view state? (Choose 2)
options: Make the list variable public
Mark the list as transient
Raise the view state limit in Session Settings
Load the read-only data with JavaScript remoting instead of storing it in the controller
Move the table inside an apex:form
questions.explain: Transient variables are not saved in view state. Remoting is stateless, so data it returns is not held in view state.
wrong: Access modifiers do not change what is serialized.
The 170 KB limit cannot be configured.
View state comes from apex:form, so this would not reduce it.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Best Practices for Improving Visualforce Performance / View State

questions.q: Both extension classes and the standard controller define a public PageReference save() method. Which save() runs when the user clicks the button?
questions.code:
<apex:page standardController="Account" extensions="AuditExt,DiscountExt">
  <apex:form>
    <apex:commandButton value="Save" action="{!save}"/>
  </apex:form>
</apex:page>
options: The standard controller's save()
DiscountExt.save(), because the last extension wins
All three run in order
AuditExt.save(), because the leftmost extension takes precedence
questions.explain: When several extensions define the same method, the one in the leftmost extension is used, and it overrides the standard controller's method.
wrong: Extensions override standard controller methods that have the same name.
Precedence goes from left to right, not right to left.
Only one method runs.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Building a Controller Extension

questions.q: A Visualforce call center page must refresh its "open calls" panel automatically every 15 seconds without reloading the whole page. Which component should be used?
options: apex:actionPoller with interval="15" and rerender set to the panel Id
apex:actionStatus
apex:actionRegion
apex:outputLink
questions.explain: actionPoller calls a controller action on a timer and can rerender part of the page.
wrong: actionStatus only shows the status of an AJAX request.
actionRegion limits which part of the form is processed. It does not run on a timer.
outputLink is a plain link.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionPoller

questions.q: Clicking Show sets showDetails to true, but the details panel never appears. What is the fix?
questions.code:
<apex:commandButton value="Show" action="{!toggle}" rerender="details"/>
<apex:outputPanel id="details" rendered="{!showDetails}">
  ...
</apex:outputPanel>
options: Add immediate="true" to the commandButton
Wrap the panel in an always-rendered apex:outputPanel with an Id, and rerender that
Mark showDetails as transient
Replace rerender with reRender="{!showDetails}" so the panel redraws whenever the flag changes
questions.explain: A component that was not rendered when the page loaded has nothing in the DOM to replace. Rerender a parent that is always rendered.
wrong: immediate skips validation. It does not fix the missing DOM element.
A transient variable would lose its value between requests.
rerender takes component Ids, not a Boolean.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Using AJAX / Partial Page Updates

questions.q: A Visualforce page with a large view state needs a fast type-ahead search. Each keystroke must send the search text to Apex and get matching records back in a JavaScript callback. Which approach is best?
options: apex:actionSupport on the input, with rerender on the results table
apex:actionFunction called on every keystroke
A static @RemoteAction method called with Visualforce.remoting.Manager.invokeAction
apex:actionPoller every second
questions.explain: JavaScript remoting does not send view state. It is asynchronous, returns the data straight to a JS callback, and is the lightest option for frequent calls.
wrong: Each request posts the large view state, which is slow.
This also posts view state on every call.
Polling wastes requests and does not react to typing.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: JavaScript Remoting for Apex Controllers

questions.q: A custom JavaScript date-picker on a Visualforce page must, when a date is picked, set a controller property, run a recalculate() action that updates other controller properties, and redraw only the totals section. Which approach fits best?
options: A @RemoteAction method called with Visualforce.remoting.Manager.invokeAction that recalculates and returns the totals
apex:actionPoller with interval="1"
An apex:commandLink with no rerender attribute
apex:actionFunction with action="{!recalculate}", rerender="totals" and an apex:param, called from the picker's JS
questions.explain: actionFunction lets custom JS call a controller action within the page's state, pass parameters with apex:param, and partially refresh the page with rerender.
wrong: Remote actions are static and stateless. They cannot update the page controller's properties or rerender components.
Polling is wasteful and does not respond to the picker.
Without rerender, the whole page refreshes, and a commandLink cannot be called from custom JS with a parameter in a clean way.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionFunction

questions.q: A Visualforce page shows a comment field with <apex:outputText value="{!comment}" escape="false"/>. A security review flags it. What is the risk?
options: SOQL injection
Cross-site scripting (XSS): user-entered HTML or script is rendered unescaped
View state tampering
Cross-site request forgery, because escape="false" also removes the page's anti-CSRF token
questions.explain: escape="false" turns off Visualforce's default HTML encoding, so stored script can run in other users' browsers.
wrong: No query is built from this value.
View state is encrypted. This issue is about output encoding.
CSRF is about forged state-changing requests. The escape attribute only affects output encoding, not CSRF protection.
questions.source: Secure Coding Guide: Cross-Site Scripting / Visualforce Developer Guide

questions.q: A Visualforce page contains the script below. How should the developer prevent script injection through the URL parameter?
questions.code:
<script>
  var acct = '{!$CurrentPage.parameters.acct}';
</script>
options: Use '{!HTMLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.acct)}'
Use '{!URLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.acct)}'
Use '{!JSENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.acct)}'
Move the script into a static resource without changing the merge field
questions.explain: In a JavaScript context, JSENCODE escapes characters such as quotes and backslashes, so the value cannot break out of the string literal.
wrong: HTML encoding does not protect a JavaScript string context.
URL encoding is for URL parameters, not JS strings.
Merge fields are not evaluated in static resources, and moving the script does not fix the encoding.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Security Tips for Apex and Visualforce (JSENCODE)

questions.q: An LWC must use a third-party charting library and call fetch() on a partner's REST endpoint directly from the browser. Both currently fail in Lightning Experience. Which two actions are needed? (Choose 2)
options: Add a <script src="https://cdn..."> tag to the template
Upload the library as a static resource and load it with loadScript from lightning/platformResourceLoader
Turn off Lightning Web Security in Session Settings
Add a Remote Site Setting for the partner endpoint
Add the partner domain as a Trusted URL (CSP) with connect-src allowed
questions.explain: CSP blocks scripts from outside Salesforce and browser connections to unknown domains. Static resources plus loadScript fix the library, and a Trusted URL allows the fetch().
wrong: LWC templates do not allow script tags, and CSP blocks CDN scripts.
LWS is not what blocks these. Turning off security is not a valid fix.
Remote Site Settings allow server-side Apex callouts, not browser requests.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Content Security Policy / Use Third-Party JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: An @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) method returns Contacts, including SSN__c, to an LWC data table. The class is declared with sharing, yet users without FLS on SSN__c can still see the values. Which two changes enforce field-level security? (Choose 2)
options: Add WITH USER_MODE to the SOQL query
Change the class to inherited sharing
Rely on Lightning Web Security to hide the field
Remove cacheable=true
Pass the query results through Security.stripInaccessible(AccessType.READABLE, records)
questions.explain: Sharing keywords control record visibility, not FLS. WITH USER_MODE enforces CRUD and FLS in the query, and stripInaccessible removes fields the user cannot read.
wrong: inherited sharing is still about record sharing, not FLS.
LWS isolates JavaScript namespaces. It does not apply data permissions.
Caching has no effect on field-level security.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Enforce User Mode / Security.stripInaccessible

questions.q: The finance team at a wholesale distributor wants a "Generate Invoice" button on Opportunity. It must produce a printable invoice that matches their paper letterhead and save the file to the record, with no third-party JavaScript library. Most users work in Lightning Experience; a few still use the desktop Outlook integration. Which solution should the developer build?
options: An LWC headless quick action that calls window.print() and saves the printed output with lightning-file-upload on the Opportunity record
A Visualforce page with renderAs="pdf", and Apex that calls getContentAsPDF() and saves the Blob as a ContentVersion on the record
An Aura component that sets renderAs="pdf" on its aura:component tag and is added as a quick action
An LWC that sets renderMode="pdf" in its js-meta.xml and is placed on the Opportunity record page
questions.explain: Visualforce is the only one of these UI technologies with a built-in PDF rendering service (renderAs="pdf"). Apex can get the rendered page as a PDF Blob with PageReference.getContentAsPDF() and save it as a file on the record.
wrong: window.print() opens the browser print dialog. It does not create a file in Salesforce, and lightning-file-upload needs the user to pick a file.
renderAs is an attribute of apex:page. Aura components have no PDF rendering option.
There is no renderMode="pdf" setting in js-meta.xml. LWC cannot render itself as a PDF.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Render a Visualforce Page as a PDF File

questions.q: A service team built a new case intake LWC and wants it to replace the standard New button on Case in Lightning Experience. The component is deployed with the configuration below, but when the admin opens Buttons, Links, and Actions > New > Lightning Experience Override, the component is not in the list. What should the developer do?
questions.code:
<LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <apiVersion>62.0</apiVersion>
  <isExposed>true</isExposed>
  <targets>
    <target>lightning__RecordPage</target>
    <target>lightning__RecordAction</target>
  </targets>
</LightningComponentBundle>
options: Add lightning__UrlAddressable to targets so the override can open the component by URL
Add a targetConfig for lightning__RecordAction with actionType="Override" and <object>Case</object>, then redeploy
Wrap the LWC in an Aura component that implements lightning:actionOverride, and pick that as the override
Set isExposed to true on the Case object's page layout and redeploy
questions.explain: Only Aura components that implement lightning:actionOverride appear in the Lightning component list for standard action overrides. Wrapping the LWC in a thin Aura component that implements that interface is the supported approach.
wrong: lightning__UrlAddressable makes the component reachable by URL. It does not make it available as a standard action override.
actionType only accepts ScreenAction or Action for quick actions. There is no Override type.
isExposed is a component setting in js-meta.xml, not a page layout setting, and it is already true.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Creating an Aura Component for Use as an Action Override

questions.q: A team is replacing an Aura force:navigateToComponent call. The target LWC, c-shipment-detail, has the lightning__UrlAddressable target, and it reads the shipment Id from the URL state. Clicking the button opens the component, but it always shows "No shipment selected". What is the cause?
options: State keys must have a namespace prefix, so the caller must pass c__shipmentId instead of shipmentId
componentName must be written in kebab case, such as c-shipment-detail
standard__component pages cannot receive state, so the Id must be stored in sessionStorage
CurrentPageReference only works on record pages, so the target must also have lightning__RecordPage
questions.explain: For a URL-addressable component, every key in the page reference state must include a namespace, such as c__shipmentId, and values must be strings. A key without a namespace is not passed to the target the way the target expects.
wrong: componentName uses the namespace__componentName format (c__shipmentDetail), which the caller already uses.
The standard__component type supports state as URL query parameters. That is how data is passed to the target.
CurrentPageReference works on any Lightning page. A record page target is not needed.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: lightning__UrlAddressable Target

questions.q: An org is moving to Lightning Experience, but a regional team will stay on Salesforce Classic for another year. The architect asks which of these requirements must still be built with Visualforce instead of an LWC or Aura component. Which two? (Choose 2)
options: A page that renders a quote as a PDF using the platform's rendering service
An item in a Lightning console app's utility bar that shows open tasks
A quick action on Account that runs custom code without opening a modal
A replacement for the standard Edit button that must work for the Salesforce Classic users
A custom screen component that collects input inside a screen flow
questions.explain: PDF rendering (renderAs="pdf") exists only in Visualforce. Aura action overrides work in Lightning Experience and the mobile app but not in Salesforce Classic, so a Classic override must be a Visualforce page.
wrong: An LWC can be a utility item with the lightning__UtilityBar target.
An LWC can be a headless quick action with the lightning__RecordAction target and actionType="Action".
An LWC can be a flow screen component with the lightning__FlowScreen target.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Standard Actions and Overrides Basics

questions.q: A logistics company has a Node.js customer portal hosted outside Salesforce. Portal users already sign in to Salesforce through OAuth. The company wants to reuse an existing custom LWC that tracks deliveries on one of the portal pages, without rewriting it. What should the developer use?
options: Add the portal domain as a CSP Trusted Site so the portal can load the component from its Lightning Experience URL
apex:includeLightning and $Lightning.createComponent() in the portal's own HTML page
An Experience Cloud LWR site with a custom domain that matches the portal
Lightning Out, which embeds Lightning web components in external, non-Salesforce web apps
questions.explain: Lightning Out (Lightning Out 2.0, or the older beta) is the feature for embedding custom Lightning web components in external apps. The external app handles authentication, which the portal already does.
wrong: CSP Trusted Sites let Salesforce pages call or load resources from other domains. They do not let an outside site host Salesforce components.
apex:includeLightning is a Visualforce component. It cannot be used in a Node.js page.
An Experience Cloud site is a separate Salesforce-hosted site. It does not put the component inside the existing Node.js portal.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Components Outside Salesforce with Lightning Out 2.0

questions.q: In a Lightning console app, an LWC in the utility bar publishes the selected customer on a message channel. A second LWC sits on the Account record page, which agents usually keep open in several workspace tabs. Only the subscriber in the focused tab updates, but every open tab must update. What should the developer change?
options: Import APPLICATION_SCOPE and pass { scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE } as the fourth argument to subscribe()
Move the subscribe() call from connectedCallback() to renderedCallback()
Publish the message with { scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE } from the utility bar component instead
Replace the message channel with a CustomEvent that has bubbles: true and composed: true
questions.explain: By default a subscriber only receives messages while it is in the active area (the focused tab or a utility item). Subscribing with APPLICATION_SCOPE lets components in background tabs receive messages too.
wrong: renderedCallback runs after every render and would create repeat subscriptions. The scope is the real problem.
Scope is set by the subscriber in subscribe(), not by the publisher.
DOM events cannot travel from the utility bar to a component in a separate tab, because the two are not in the same DOM tree.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Define the Scope of the Message Service

questions.q: A field sales team wants a "Nearby Visits" component. On Lightning app pages it must appear only on phones. On Account record pages it must appear on both desktop and phone. Which js-meta.xml configuration meets this?

    <supportedFormFactors>
      <supportedFormFactor type="..."/>
    </supportedFormFactors>
  </targetConfig>
</targetConfigs>
options: One targetConfig for "lightning__AppPage,lightning__RecordPage" with supportedFormFactor type="Small" only
A targetConfig for lightning__AppPage with type="Small", and a targetConfig for lightning__RecordPage with type="Large" and type="Small"
A targetConfig for lightning__AppPage with type="Phone", and a targetConfig for lightning__RecordPage with type="Desktop" and type="Phone"
A supportedFormFactors block directly under <targets>, listing type="Small" for app pages and type="Medium" for record pages
questions.explain: supportedFormFactors goes inside each targetConfig, so each page type can have its own devices. The valid values are Large (desktop) and Small (phone).
wrong: A shared targetConfig would limit the record page to phones too, so desktop users would lose the component.
Phone and Desktop are not valid types. The values are Small and Large.
supportedFormFactors is not allowed directly under targets, and Medium is not a supported value for page form factors.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure Your Component for Different Form Factors

questions.q: A developer wants a compact card layout for phone users of the Salesforce mobile app and the full table on desktop. Testers on phones always see the full table. What is the bug?
options: formFactor must be read in connectedCallback(), because the module value is not ready when the getter runs
The value for a phone is 'PHONE', the same as $Browser.formFactor in Aura
The value for a phone is 'Small', so the getter should compare FORM_FACTOR to 'Small'
Getters are not reactive, so isPhone must be a field decorated with @track
questions.explain: @salesforce/client/formFactor returns Large for desktop, Medium for tablet and Small for phone. Comparing to 'Phone' is never true.
wrong: The imported value is available as soon as the module loads, so a getter can read it at any time.
PHONE is a value from the Aura $Browser value provider, not from the LWC formFactor module.
The getter returns a constant value. Reactivity is not the issue, and @track would not change the comparison.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Client Form Factor

questions.q: On a phone, the two panels below appear squeezed side by side instead of stacked. On desktops they should sit side by side at half width each. Which two changes fix the layout? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<lightning-layout>
  <lightning-layout-item medium-device-size="6" padding="around-small">
    <c-account-summary></c-account-summary>
  </lightning-layout-item>
  <lightning-layout-item medium-device-size="6" padding="around-small">
    <c-open-cases></c-open-cases>
  </lightning-layout-item>
</lightning-layout>
options: Replace medium-device-size="6" with small-device-size="12" only
Add size="12" to each lightning-layout-item
Add flexibility="auto" to lightning-layout
Wrap each item in a div with class slds-hide_medium
Add multiple-rows="true" to lightning-layout so items can wrap onto new rows
questions.explain: The device-size attributes only work when size is also set; size="12" makes each item full width on phones, and medium-device-size="6" applies from tablets up. multiple-rows="true" lets full-width items wrap onto new rows instead of squeezing into one.
wrong: small-device-size still needs size to be set, and it would make items full width on larger screens too.
flexibility is an attribute of lightning-layout-item, and auto sizing does not force items to stack.
slds-hide_medium hides content on medium screens and up, which would remove the panels from desktops.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-layout-item

questions.q: An Aura component on a record page should show a short summary on phones and a detailed view on desktop. On phones it always shows the detailed view. Which two changes would make the phone check work? (Choose 2)
questions.code:

Compare $Browser.formFactor to 'small' in lowercase
Compare $Browser.formFactor to 'PHONE'
Use {!$Browser.isPhone} as the condition
Add a design:supportedFormFactor of type Small to the component's .design file
questions.explain: In Aura, $Browser.formFactor returns enum values such as DESKTOP and PHONE, and $Browser.isPhone is true on phones. Small/Large belong to the LWC formFactor module and to page configuration.
wrong: @salesforce scoped modules are for Lightning web components, not Aura controllers.
The value is PHONE, so changing the case of 'Small' does not help.
The design file controls on which devices App Builder shows the component, not which markup it renders.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: $Browser

questions.q: A Visualforce page styled with apex:slds shows a set of product tiles. Product owners want one tile per row on phones, two per row on tablets and three per row on desktops. Each tile is a div inside a parent div. Which classes should the developer use?

Parent: slds-container_fluid; tile: slds-col slds-max-small-size_1-of-1

questions.q: An Aura wrapper contains an LWC that lets agents pick a warranty plan. The LWC dispatches the event below. Which line in the Aura controller correctly reads the selected plan Id?
options: component.get('v.planId')
event.getSource().get('v.selectedPlanId')
event.target.value
event.getParam('planId')
questions.explain: When an Aura component handles a DOM event from an LWC, the properties in the event's detail object are read with event.getParam(), such as event.getParam('planId').
wrong: This reads the wrapper's own attribute, which has not been set yet.
selectedPlanId is a private field of the LWC, not an Aura attribute, so it cannot be read this way.
event.target.value is for native input events. The data is in the custom event's detail.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Send Events to an Enclosing Aura Component

questions.q: An Aura app page component contains an LWC with an @api method called loadDefaults(). The Aura component calls it from its init handler, but the browser console shows an error and the defaults never load. What is the cause?
questions.code:
<!-- quoteShell.cmp -->
<aura:component implements="flexipage:availableForAllPageTypes">
  <aura:handler name="init" value="{!this}" action="{!c.doInit}"/>
  <c:quoteLines aura:id="lines"/>
</aura:component>

// quoteShellController.js
doInit: function (component) {
  component.find('lines').loadDefaults();
}
options: Aura cannot call LWC methods. The LWC must listen for an Aura application event instead
The LWC is not created until the Aura component renders, so its method cannot be called during init
aura:id does not work on LWCs. The method must be found with document.querySelector('c-quote-lines')
The method name must be in kebab case, such as component.find('lines')['load-defaults']()
questions.explain: An Aura component can call an LWC's @api method with component.find(), but Lightning web components are not created until the Aura component renders. Calling the method during init fails.
wrong: Aura can call an LWC's public method through component.find('auraId').methodName().
aura:id works on LWCs inside Aura markup, and document queries break component encapsulation.
JavaScript methods keep their camel case name. Kebab case is only for HTML attributes.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compose Aura Components from Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A Reset button in an Aura wrapper should clear the filters in a child LWC. Clicking it throws "component.find(...).clearFilters is not a function". What should the developer change?
options: Decorate clearFilters() with @api so the parent can call it
Rename the method to setClearFilters() so Aura treats it as a setter
Fire an Aura component event from the wrapper and handle it in the LWC with aura:handler
Change objectName to a method so Aura sees the component as public
questions.explain: Only methods decorated with @api are public. An Aura or LWC parent can call a child method only when it is public.
wrong: Aura does not treat method names starting with set as public methods.
An LWC cannot use aura:handler or handle Aura component events.
Having one public property does not make other methods public. Each method needs @api.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compose Aura Components from Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An LWC (c-region-picker) sits inside Aura component A, which is inside Aura component B. The picker dispatches a regionchange event. Component B must react, but a handler that B puts on its <c:componentA> tag never runs. Which two approaches work? (Choose 2)
options: Handle onregionchange on the <c:regionPicker> tag in component A, then fire an Aura component event that B handles
Dispatch the event with bubbles: true and composed: true so B's onregionchange handler on <c:componentA> catches it
Publish the region on a Lightning message channel from the LWC and subscribe in B with lightning:messageChannel
Add <aura:handler name="regionchange" action="{!c.handle}"/> to component B
Register the event in the LWC with <aura:registerEvent name="regionchange" type="c:regionEvt"/>
questions.explain: An onxxx handler for an LWC DOM event can only be set in the first Aura component the event reaches. That component can pass the data on with an Aura event. Lightning Message Service also works across LWC and Aura without depending on nesting.
wrong: The docs say the handler can only be specified in the first Aura component the DOM event bubbles to, so B still cannot use onregionchange.
aura:handler with a name handles Aura component events, not DOM events from an LWC.
aura:registerEvent is Aura markup. LWCs have no equivalent and cannot fire Aura events.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Send Events to an Enclosing Aura Component

questions.q: A Visualforce page on an Account Lightning record page subscribes to a message channel that an LWC publishes on. The page updates correctly in Lightning Experience on desktop, but sales reps say it never updates in the Salesforce mobile app. What is the most likely reason?

<apex:page>
  <script>
    var CHANNEL = "{!$MessageChannel.Account_Selected__c}";
    var sub;
    function startListening() {
      if (!sub) {
        sub = sforce.one.subscribe(CHANNEL, onAccount, { scope: "APPLICATION" });
      }
    }
    function onAccount(msg) { /* update the page */ }
    startListening();
  </script>
</apex:page>
options: The channel must be referenced as $MessageChannel.Account_Selected instead of with the __c suffix on mobile
The scope option must be removed, because APPLICATION scope is not allowed on mobile
The LWC must publish with sforce.one.publish() so that the Visualforce page can receive it
Lightning Message Service supports Aura and LWC in the Salesforce mobile app, but not Visualforce pages
questions.explain: Lightning Message Service works in the Salesforce mobile app for Aura and Lightning web components only. Visualforce pages there cannot send or receive messages, so the code itself is not the problem.
wrong: The channel API name always uses the __c suffix, on every device.
Removing the scope does not help, because Visualforce is not supported in the mobile app at all.
An LWC publishes with publish() from lightning/messageService. sforce.one is the Visualforce API.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lightning Message Service Limitations

questions.q: An Aura component must publish the selected order on the Order_Selected__c message channel when a button is clicked. Clicking the button throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'publish')". What is the fix?

<aura:component>

}

Call $A.get('e.c:Order_Selected__c').fire() instead of publish()
Add aura:id="orderChannel" to the lightning:messageChannel tag
Set scope="APPLICATION" on lightning:messageChannel
questions.explain: In Aura, the component finds the lightning:messageChannel by its aura:id and calls publish() on it. Without the aura:id, cmp.find() returns undefined.
wrong: ES module imports from @salesforce are for LWCs. Aura uses the lightning:messageChannel component.
A message channel is not an Aura application event, so it cannot be fired with $A.get().
scope controls which subscribers receive messages. It does not fix the missing reference.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Publish on a Message Channel

questions.q: A developer uploaded chart.js as a zip static resource named chartjs_v4. Inside the zip the file is at dist/chart.umd.js. The LWC below shows the error toast on every page load, and the network tab shows a 404 for the script. What is the fix?
