Import the file directly with import CHARTJS from '@salesforce/resourceUrl/chartjs_v4/dist/chart.umd.js'
Move loadScript() into connectedCallback(), because renderedCallback() runs too late for libraries
Upload the file again as a separate static resource, because loadScript cannot read files inside a zip
questions.explain: The imported resource URL points to the archive itself, so the path inside the zip is added with string concatenation and must start with a slash. Without it the URL is wrong and the request returns 404.
wrong: The import names the static resource only. The path inside the archive is added at runtime.
Loading in renderedCallback() with a guard flag is the documented pattern, and it does not cause a 404.
loadScript can load a file from an archive static resource when the path is built correctly.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Static Resources

questions.q: A team is planning how to package front-end assets (a 3 MB mapping library, icons and a stylesheet) as static resources for LWC, Aura and Visualforce pages, some of which are used on a public Experience Cloud site. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: An LWC can load the library by adding <script src={libUrl}></script> to its template once the URL is imported
A single static resource can be up to 5 MB, and an org can hold up to 250 MB of static resources
In a Salesforce DX project, assets can be grouped into subfolders of the staticresources folder, one per library
With Cache Control set to Public, the cached resource can be reached by all internet traffic, including unauthenticated users
A static resource name such as map-lib-v2 is valid as long as it is unique in the org
questions.explain: The documented limits are 5 MB per static resource and 250 MB per org. Public cache control shares the cached data and makes it reachable by unauthenticated traffic, which matters for public sites.
wrong: LWC templates cannot contain script tags. Libraries are loaded with loadScript from lightning/platformResourceLoader.
The docs say you cannot create subdirectories of staticresources. Use a zip archive to keep a folder structure.
Names can contain only letters, numbers and underscores, so hyphens are not allowed.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Static Resources

questions.q: A field service Visualforce page needs a signature pad library. The developer uploaded a zip static resource named SignaturePad that contains js/signature_pad.min.js. Which markup loads the script correctly?
options: <apex:includeScript value="{!$Resource.SignaturePad.js.signature_pad}"/>
<ltng:require scripts="{!$Resource.SignaturePad + '/js/signature_pad.min.js'}"/>
<apex:includeScript value="{!$Resource['SignaturePad/js/signature_pad.min.js']}"/>
<apex:includeScript value="{!URLFOR($Resource.SignaturePad, 'js/signature_pad.min.js')}"/>
questions.explain: In Visualforce, a file inside an archive static resource is referenced with URLFOR(), passing the resource and the path inside the archive. $Resource.name alone is for stand-alone files.
wrong: Merge fields cannot walk into a zip with dot notation.
ltng:require is an Aura tag. It is not used in Visualforce pages.
The $Resource key is the resource name only. The path inside the archive is not part of the name.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Referencing a Static Resource in Visualforce Markup

questions.q: An Aura component draws a heat map with two libraries from the mapLibs zip: leaflet.js, and heat.js, which depends on leaflet. Users see "L is not defined" in the console and the map never draws. Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
questions.code: // controller doInit: function (component) { var map = L.map(component.find('map').getElement()); }
options: Put each library in its own ltng:require tag so they load separately and in order
Add <script src="{!$Resource.mapLibs + '/leaflet.js'}"/> above the ltng:require tag
Build the scripts value with join(',', $Resource.mapLibs + '/leaflet.js', $Resource.mapLibs + '/heat.js')
Call loadScript() from lightning/platformResourceLoader in the Aura controller instead
Remove the init handler and run the map code from afterScriptsLoaded="{!c.initMap}" on ltng:require
questions.explain: Several $Resource references in one attribute must be combined with join(). Scripts load asynchronously, so code that uses them belongs in the afterScriptsLoaded action, not in init.
wrong: Separate ltng:require tags load in parallel, so heat.js could load before leaflet.js.
Aura components cannot contain script tags.
lightning/platformResourceLoader is an LWC module. Aura uses ltng:require.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Using External JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: A Lightning record page has an older Aura component that loads a charting library with ltng:require, and a new LWC that loads the same file with loadScript. Both use the same static resource URL. After the LWC renders, the Aura chart loses the plugins it had registered on the library's global object. What explains this?
options: ltng:require loads its scripts again each time the Aura component rerenders, which wipes the plugins it registered
Archive static resources are unpacked again on every request, which resets the global object
ltng:require and loadScript don't detect each other, so the file runs twice; load it once or check its global
Static resources with Private cache control are downloaded again for each component on the page
questions.explain: The platform does not detect duplicates between ltng:require and loadScript for the same URL, so the script runs twice and replaces the global. The script must protect itself, for example by checking for an existing global.
wrong: Scripts in ltng:require load only once, even across several components.
How the archive is stored does not reset JavaScript globals. Running the script a second time does.
Cache control affects server-side caching between users, not how often a script runs on a page.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning/platformResourceLoader

questions.q: A component shows a renewal record with getRecord. When users open it for a record they cannot access, the error banner shows up empty instead of with a message. What change fixes the banner?
options: Read error.message instead, because wire adapters throw standard JavaScript Error objects
Read the message from error.statusText, because LDS puts the message there for 4xx errors
Wrap the handler in try/catch, because wire errors are thrown instead of being passed in error
Check Array.isArray(error.body) and join the message of each item, falling back to error.body.message
questions.explain: UI API read operations such as getRecord return error.body as an array of objects, while Apex and write errors return an object. A reduceErrors-style helper handles both shapes.
wrong: LDS errors are FetchResponse objects with body, ok, status and statusText, not plain Error objects.
statusText holds the status code text, such as NOT_FOUND, not the user-facing message.
The wire service passes the error in the error property. A try/catch around the handler does not change the body shape.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors in Lightning Data Service

questions.q: A security review of a payment LWC found that when the Apex method fails, the browser receives the Apex class name and line details in error.body.stackTrace. The team wants users to see a short, clear message and no internal details. What should the developer do?
options: Wrap the JavaScript call in try/catch so the stack trace is not sent to the browser
Catch it in Apex and throw new AuraHandledException('We could not apply this payment.')
Define PaymentException extends Exception and throw it with the same message from a catch block
Mark the method cacheable=true so errors are served from the client cache without server details
questions.explain: An AuraHandledException returns your own message to the client and its error does not include body.stackTrace. Unhandled exceptions are sent to the client as they are.
wrong: A client-side try/catch only handles the error after the browser has already received it.
A custom exception that is not handled still sends the class name and line number to the client.
A method that performs DML cannot be cacheable, and caching does not hide error details.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors from Apex

questions.q: An Aura component calls an Apex method that throws AuraHandledException('Credit limit exceeded'). The error toast appears, but it says "undefined". What is the bug?
options: response.getError() returns an array, so the message is in errors[0].message
AuraHandledException sets the state to INCOMPLETE, so the message is never in the ERROR branch
The message is only available from response.getReturnValue() when the state is ERROR
AuraHandledException messages are only sent to Lightning web components, not to Aura components
questions.explain: When Apex throws an AuraHandledException, the state is ERROR and response.getError() returns an array of error objects. The custom message is in errors[0].message.
wrong: INCOMPLETE means the server could not be reached. A thrown AuraHandledException gives the state ERROR.
getReturnValue() holds the result of a successful call, not error details.
AuraHandledException was designed for Aura client controllers and also works for LWC.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Returning Errors from an Apex Server-Side Controller

questions.q: On a Visualforce order page, applyCoupon() adds an error message when the coupon has expired. The totals panel refreshes, but users never see the error. Which two changes would show the message? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<apex:form>
  <apex:pageMessages/>
  <apex:inputText value="{!couponCode}"/>
  <apex:commandButton value="Apply" action="{!applyCoupon}" rerender="totals"/>
  <apex:outputPanel id="totals">{!orderTotal}</apex:outputPanel>
</apex:form>

// controller
public PageReference applyCoupon() {
  if (couponIsExpired(couponCode)) {
    ApexPages.addMessage(new ApexPages.Message(
      ApexPages.Severity.ERROR, 'This coupon has expired.'));
  }
  return null;
}
options: Give apex:pageMessages an id such as "msgs" and set rerender="totals,msgs"
Add immediate="true" to the command button so messages are sent first
Return new PageReference('/apex/OrderPage').setRedirect(true) after adding the message
Change the severity to FATAL so the message is shown even during partial refresh
Move apex:pageMessages inside the totals output panel
questions.explain: In a partial page refresh, only the components in rerender are redrawn. The message component must be rerendered too, either by adding its id to rerender or by placing it inside a rerendered panel.
wrong: immediate skips applying input values, so the coupon code would not reach the controller. It does not rerender the messages.
A redirect starts a new request, and messages from the previous request are lost.
Severity changes the style of the message, not whether the component is redrawn.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:pageMessages

questions.q: A partner self-registration LWC runs in an LWR Experience Cloud site. When the Apex save fails, the catch block below runs (the console log confirms it), but no toast appears on the page. What should the developer do?
options: Add mode: 'sticky' so the toast stays visible until it is closed
Create the event with bubbles: true and composed: true so the site shell receives it
Import Toast from 'lightning/toast' and call Toast.show({ label, message, variant: 'error' }, this)
Add a lightning/toastContainer instance to the page, because ShowToastEvent needs a container in LWR sites
questions.explain: lightning/platformShowToastEvent is not supported in LWR sites for Experience Cloud. lightning/toast is the recommended module, and it creates its own page-level toast container.
wrong: The mode controls how long a toast stays. No toast is shown at all in an LWR site.
Event propagation is not the problem. LWR sites do not handle ShowToastEvent.
A toast container cannot make an unsupported module work in an LWR site.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Toast Notifications

questions.q: A custom two-column lightning-record-edit-form saves Contracts. When a validation rule blocks the save, nothing happens on screen and users think the button is broken. The team wants server errors to show in the form automatically, without writing an error handler, and must keep its custom markup (a grid with section headings and help text between the fields). A lightning-messages component placed just before or after the input fields
required on every lightning-input-field so errors are caught before submit
Replace the form with lightning-record-form, which shows errors automatically
questions.explain: lightning-messages inside lightning-record-edit-form automatically shows the error message returned on submit, including validation rule errors, without a custom handler.
wrong: This works, but it is a custom error handler, which the team wants to avoid.
required only checks for empty fields on the client. It cannot catch validation rule errors from the server.
lightning-record-form generates its own layout, so the custom markup between the fields would be lost.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-record-edit-form

questions.q: A custom controller page lets users update an Account. When a validation rule (error location: top of page) fails, users get a full-page Visualforce error with FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION instead of a friendly message on the form. Which two changes together show the error on the page? (Choose 2)

  return null;
}

Wrap the update in try/catch (DmlException ex) and call ApexPages.addMessages(ex)
Add <apex:pageMessages/> (or apex:messages) to the page
Return new PageReference(ApexPages.currentPage().getUrl()).setRedirect(true) from save()
Set escape="false" on the inputField components so the error text can render
questions.explain: With a custom controller, the controller must catch the DML exception and add it to the page messages. The page then needs a messages component to display errors whose location is the top of the page.
wrong: AuraHandledException is for Lightning components. In Visualforce it is still an unhandled exception.
A redirect starts a new request, so any message would be lost and the user's edits too.
apex:inputField has no escape attribute, and escaping is not why the error is missing.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Validation Rules and Custom Controllers

questions.q: A related contacts LWC on the Account record page always shows "No contacts", even for accounts with many contacts. Debug logs show the Apex method runs with accountId = 'recordId'. What should the developer change?
options: Change the config to { accountId: this.recordId }
Decorate recordId with @track as well as @api
Change the config to { accountId: '$recordId' }
Rename the Apex parameter to recordId so it matches the property name
questions.explain: Without the $ prefix the wire passes the literal string 'recordId'. '$recordId' tells the wire service to use the property value and to call the method again when it changes.
wrong: In a @wire config, this does not refer to the component instance, and the value would not be reactive.
@api fields are already reactive. The problem is the literal string.
The Apex parameter name must match the config key (accountId), which it already does.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An admin adds the "Open Cases" LWC to both the Account record page and the Home page. On the record page it works. On the Home page it shows the loading spinner forever, and no error appears in the console or the debug logs. Why?
options: The Home page has no record, so recordId is undefined, and the wire won't call Apex while a parameter is undefined
Apex throws a NullPointerException for the null Id, and cacheable methods hide server errors from the client
@wire only runs on record pages, so the component must call getOpenCases imperatively on other pages
The cached result from the record page is locked to that page, so the Home page waits until the cache entry expires
questions.explain: If a wire parameter is undefined, the Apex method is not called, so neither data nor error is ever provisioned. The component should handle the missing recordId, for example by showing a message instead of the spinner.
wrong: The method is never called, so there is no Apex exception. Cacheable methods do return errors to the client.
@wire works on any page. It only waits because the parameter is undefined.
The client cache is keyed by parameters and does not block other pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: After a user adds a line item, the totals panel still shows the old amount until the page is reloaded. getTotals is @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) and addLine is @AuraEnabled without cacheable. Which two changes would make the totals refresh? (Choose 2)
options: Call refreshApex(this.totals) after addLine() resolves
Mark addLine as cacheable=true so both methods share one cache entry and refresh each other
Decorate totals with @track so the template sees the new values
Remove cacheable=true from getTotals so every imperative call goes to the server
Wire getTotals with { quoteId: '$recordId' }, keep the provisioned value, and pass it to refreshApex() after addLine() resolves
questions.explain: Calling a cacheable method imperatively checks the client cache first, so the same parameters can return the cached result. Either make the call non-cacheable, or wire the method and refresh the wired value with refreshApex().
wrong: refreshApex() only works with a value that an Apex @wire provisioned, not with the result of an imperative call.
addLine performs DML, so it cannot be cacheable.
The property is reassigned, so it is already reactive. The value itself is stale.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Client-Side Caching of Apex Method Results

questions.q: A product picker lets users tick products before adding them to a quote. Ticking a checkbox throws an "Invalid mutation ... is read-only" error in the console. What is the best fix?
options: Decorate products with @track so its nested properties can be changed
Copy the records as they arrive: this.products = data.map((p) => ({ ...p, selected: false }))
Call refreshApex() before changing the record so the wire cache is unlocked and the objects become writable
Move the assignment of this.products into renderedCallback()
questions.explain: The wire service provisions an immutable stream of data, and the objects it passes are read-only. To change them, the component makes a shallow copy.
wrong: @track does not make the read-only objects from the wire service writable.
refreshApex() gets fresh data from the server. The new data is read-only as well.
Where the assignment happens does not matter. The objects themselves are read-only.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Understand the Wire Service

questions.q: An order dashboard LWC displays the result of the Apex method below. The order number and total show correctly, but the Status column is always empty, even though debug logs show status is set on every object. What is the cause?
options: The status property is not annotated with @AuraEnabled, so it is not serialized to the client
Status is a restricted picklist, so it must be converted with String.valueOf() first
Wrapper classes must be declared without sharing for all their properties to be returned
The query needs WITH USER_MODE, otherwise picklist fields are removed from wrapper objects
questions.explain: When an Apex object is returned to a component, only properties annotated with @AuraEnabled are serialized. status is missing the annotation, so the client never receives it.
wrong: Order.Status is already a String in Apex. No conversion is needed.
Sharing affects which records the query returns, not which properties are serialized.
USER_MODE enforces the user's permissions. It does not decide which wrapper properties are sent.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Returning Data from an Apex Server-Side Controller

questions.q: Compliance wants every view of the pricing panel to be logged. A developer adds an insert to the wired Apex method below. Now the panel shows an error instead of prices. Which change meets both needs and keeps the wire?
options: Use Database.insert(log, false) so a failed insert does not stop the query or the wire from returning
Declare the class without sharing so the insert is allowed in a cacheable method
Keep getPrices read-only and log the view in a separate non-cacheable method called imperatively
Pass { cacheable: false } in the @wire configuration object for this call
questions.explain: A cacheable method must only read data, so it cannot perform DML. Logging belongs in a separate method without cacheable=true, called imperatively, while the wire keeps using the read-only method.
wrong: Database.insert is still DML, which is not allowed in a cacheable method.
Sharing does not change the rule that cacheable methods cannot change data.
The wire config only passes method parameters. Cacheability is set on the Apex annotation, and @wire requires cacheable=true.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Client-Side Caching of Apex Method Results

questions.q: A shipping-rate LWC uses a Continuation because the carrier API can take up to 40 seconds. The component wires startRequest. What happens when the component loads?
options: It works, but the response is not cached on the client
It fails to compile, because continuation=true and cacheable=true must be separated by a comma in @AuraEnabled
It works only for imperative calls, and the wire silently provisions nothing
It throws an exception: if the Continuation method is cacheable, the callback must be cacheable=true too
questions.explain: For continuations, a cacheable starting method with a non-cacheable callback is not a valid combination and throws an exception. Setting cacheable=true on all methods in the chain makes it valid and usable with @wire.
wrong: The docs list this exact combination as invalid. It does not just skip caching.
The attributes are separated by a space, as in continuation=true cacheable=true.
The combination is invalid, so it is not a choice between wire and imperative calls.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: @AuraEnabled Annotations for Continuations

questions.q: On a Visualforce page for Opportunity, changing Stage should redraw the forecast panel. Instead, users who have not entered a Close Date yet see "Close Date: You must enter a value" and the panel does not update. What should the developer do?
questions.code:
<apex:page standardController="Opportunity" extensions="ForecastExt">
  <apex:form>
    <apex:pageBlock id="block">
      <apex:inputField value="{!Opportunity.CloseDate}"/>
      <apex:inputField value="{!Opportunity.StageName}">
        <apex:actionSupport event="onchange" action="{!recalcForecast}" rerender="forecast"/>
      </apex:inputField>
      <apex:outputPanel id="forecast">{!forecastText}</apex:outputPanel>
    </apex:pageBlock>
  </apex:form>
</apex:page>
options: Add immediate="true" to the actionSupport so validation is skipped
Change rerender="forecast" to rerender="block" so the whole block is redrawn
Set required="false" on the Close Date inputField
Wrap the Stage inputField and its actionSupport in an apex:actionRegion
questions.explain: apex:actionRegion limits which components the server processes in the AJAX request. Only the Stage field is submitted and validated, so the empty Close Date does not block the request, and the new Stage reaches the controller.
wrong: immediate skips validation but also does not apply the new Stage value, so the forecast would use stale data.
rerender controls what is redrawn, not what is processed, so the validation error stays.
Close Date is a required field on Opportunity, and the business still needs it on save.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionRegion

questions.q: Sales reps change the quantity, then click Recalculate. The summary panel redraws, but it still shows the totals for the old quantity. What is the cause?
questions.code:
<apex:inputText value="{!quantity}"/>
<apex:commandButton value="Recalculate" action="{!recalculate}"
                    immediate="true" rerender="summary"/>
<apex:outputPanel id="summary">Total: {!total}</apex:outputPanel>

// controller
public Integer quantity { get; set; }
public Decimal total { get; private set; }
public PageReference recalculate() {
  total = quantity * unitPrice;
  return null;
}
options: total has a private setter, so the page cannot show the new value
immediate="true" skips updating the data model, so the quantity setter never gets the new value
rerender only works on apex:outputPanel elements that also have layout="block", so the panel keeps old values
inputText cannot bind to an Integer property; it must use apex:inputField
questions.explain: With immediate="true", the action runs without applying the submitted values to the controller, so recalculate() still sees the old quantity. immediate is meant for actions like Cancel that leave the page.
wrong: A private setter only stops the page from writing total. The controller can still set it, and the getter is public.
rerender works with any component that has an id, whatever its layout.
apex:inputText can bind to controller properties that are not sObject fields, such as an Integer.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Use the immediate Attribute Carefully

questions.q: A developer wants a Remove button on each row of an order lines table, using the markup below in a page at API version 60.0. The markup breaks a rule for apex:actionFunction. Which change fixes it?
questions.code: {!l.Name}
options: Replace the actionFunction with a @RemoteAction method, which can rerender the lines panel
Add immediate="true" to the actionFunction so the parameter is assigned first
Move the apex:actionFunction after the apex:repeat, still inside the apex:form
Move the apex:actionFunction outside the apex:form so it is defined only once
questions.explain: Since API version 23, apex:actionFunction cannot be placed inside an iteration component. Define it once after the iteration, inside the form, and call it from each row with the parameter.
wrong: Remote actions are static and cannot rerender Visualforce components.
immediate would skip applying values, and the placement problem would remain.
apex:actionFunction must be a child of an apex:form.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionFunction

questions.q: A warranty lookup button on a Visualforce page calls a slow external service that takes about 20 seconds. At month end, hundreds of agents click it at once and many get errors about too many concurrent long-running requests. What should the developer change in the controller?
options: Return a Continuation from the action, with continuationMethod set to a callback that reads the response
Move the callout into an @future(callout=true) method and set warrantyStatus from it
Lower req.setTimeout() to 5000 so each request finishes faster
Call the method with JavaScript remoting and { timeout: 120000 } so the wait runs outside the page request
questions.explain: With a Continuation, the callout is handed to the Continuation server and the request is suspended, so it does not count toward the concurrent long-running request limit. The callback method processes the response when it returns.
wrong: A future method runs later in its own transaction and cannot set a value on the page that is waiting.
A shorter timeout makes calls fail sooner. It does not make the service faster.
The server still holds the request open while it waits for the slow service, so it still counts as a long-running request.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Make Long-Running Callouts with Continuations

questions.q: A tag picker shows "{count} selected". Users tick tags, but the count stays at 0. What should the developer change?
options: Replace @track with @api so the parent component can observe the Set and push its new size back down to the child
After each change, assign a new Set, e.g. this.selected = new Set(this.selected), as Set mutations aren't observed
Move the add() and delete() calls into renderedCallback() so that every change happens inside the render cycle
Keep @track and add this.selected = this.selected after each change so the engine sees an assignment to the field
questions.explain: LWC observes mutations inside plain objects and arrays, but not inside complex objects such as Set, Map, Date or class instances, even with @track. Assigning a new Set gives the field a new reference, so the component rerenders.
wrong: @api makes the property public and read-only to the child; it doesn't make Set mutations observable.
Changing state in renderedCallback() is an anti-pattern and still mutates the same Set, which isn't observed.
Assigning the same reference is === to the old value, so the engine doesn't rerender.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Field Reactivity

questions.q: A reviewer flags the list template below. Contacts can be added and removed, and the first and last rows get special styling. What should change?
options: Use a unique value from the data as the key, such as key={it.value.Id}, since the index can't be a key
Move key={it.index} from the li element onto the template tag that holds the iterator directive
Replace iterator with for:each, because the iterator directive doesn't support lwc:if on its items
Replace it.last with a check of it.index against contacts.length - 1, because the iterator has no last property
questions.explain: Every list item needs a key that is a unique string or number from the data, and the docs say you can't use the index as the key. The iterator directive does provide value, index, first and last.
wrong: The key goes on the first element inside the nested template, not on the template tag, and an index is still not allowed.
lwc:if works inside an iterator; first and last are exactly why you choose iterator.
The iterator directive exposes first and last as booleans.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Render Lists

questions.q: A child LWC must round the amount its parent passes in, every time the parent changes it. The developer writes the code below, and the component fails to save. What is the fix?
options: Remove the getter, because a public property only needs a setter when the parent is the one that writes it
Rename _amount to amount, so the getter and the setter share the public property as their own backing field
Replace both with @track amount and do the rounding once in connectedCallback() when the component loads
Keep @api on only one of the two, by convention the getter, because a getter and setter can't both have it
questions.explain: A public property with a custom setter must also have a getter, and only one of them is annotated with @api. The docs annotate the getter and keep the value in a private field such as _amount.
wrong: A setter for a public property must have a matching getter.
Using the property's own name as its backing field would recurse into the getter and setter.
connectedCallback runs once, so later changes from the parent wouldn't be rounded, and @track doesn't make it public.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Getters and Setters to Modify Data

questions.q: Two agents often edit the same Case in this custom LWC. The business wants a save to fail, instead of silently overwriting, if someone else saved the Case after the component loaded it. What should the developer do?
options: Call notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([this.recordId]) just before updateRecord, so LDS loads the latest copy of the Case first
Add apiName: 'Case' to the recordInput, so the UI API compares record versions before it applies the update
Wire LastModifiedDate with getRecord and pass { ifUnmodifiedSince: lastModifiedDate } as updateRecord's clientOptions
Call refreshApex on the wired record before saving, then compare the old and new Status values in JavaScript
questions.explain: updateRecord takes clientOptions with ifUnmodifiedSince set to the LastModifiedDate read through a wire adapter. If the record changed since then, the update is rejected instead of overwriting the other agent's work.
wrong: This refreshes cached data but still overwrites whatever the other agent saved.
apiName is only for creating records; for an update you pass null or leave it out.
refreshApex is for wired Apex results, not getRecord, and a client-side comparison still leaves a race window.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: updateRecord(recordInput, clientOptions)

questions.q: A deal summary LWC wires getRecord for Opportunity Amount and CloseDate and shows them with getFieldValue. Users see 125000 and 2026-12-31 instead of formatted currency and dates. The team wants formatted, localized values with no formatting code. What should the developer do?
options: Move both fields into optionalFields, because optional fields are returned already formatted for display to the user
Show the values with getFieldDisplayValue(this.deal.data, AMOUNT_FIELD), which returns the formatted display value
Switch the wire to layoutTypes: ['Full'], which returns every field on the layout as a formatted string
Pass { formatted: true } as a third argument to getFieldValue, so it returns the display value instead
questions.explain: getFieldDisplayValue returns the field's display value, which is formatted and localized, while getFieldValue returns the raw value. The same data is available as record.data.fields.Amount.displayValue.
wrong: optionalFields only changes what happens when the user can't see a field; values aren't formatted differently.
layoutTypes chooses which fields come back, not whether they are formatted.
getFieldValue has no formatting option; getFieldDisplayValue is the separate function for this.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: getFieldDisplayValue(record, field)

questions.q: A Quick Note button in an LWC on an Account page must create a Task related to the Account with Lightning Data Service and no Apex. Which call is correct?
options: createRecord(TASK_OBJECT, { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId })
updateRecord({ apiName: 'Task', fields: { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })
createRecord({ fields: { attributes: { type: 'Task' }, Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })
createRecord({ apiName: 'Task', fields: { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })
questions.explain: createRecord takes one recordInput object with the object's apiName and a fields map. updateRecord only updates existing records, identified by the Id in fields.
wrong: createRecord takes a single recordInput object, not the object and fields as separate arguments.
updateRecord doesn't create records; for an update, apiName is left out and fields must contain the Id.
The object is named with apiName, not with an attributes block inside fields.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: createRecord(recordInput); updateRecord(recordInput, clientOptions)

questions.q: A Visualforce page shows only {!opportunity.Name} and {!maxDiscount}. It fails with "SObject row was retrieved via SOQL without querying the requested field: Opportunity.Amount". Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
options: Call std.addFields(new List<String>{ 'Amount', 'Discount_Cap__c' }) in the constructor before getRecord()
Declare the extension without sharing, so the standard controller is allowed to load every field on the record
Reference both fields on the page in a hidden component, such as an apex:outputText with rendered="false"
Call std.reset() inside getMaxDiscount() just before reading the fields, so the record is queried again in full
Read the record with std.getRecord().clone(true, true), because a deep clone copies every field from the database
questions.explain: A standard controller loads only the fields referenced in the page markup. addFields() in the constructor adds more, and a hidden component that references the fields (rendered="false") is the documented workaround.
wrong: Sharing keywords control record access, not which fields the standard controller loads.
reset() is only needed before calling addFields outside the constructor; on its own it adds no fields.
clone() copies the fields already in memory; it doesn't query new ones.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: StandardController Class (addFields, getRecord)

questions.q: A Visualforce mass-update page builds its StandardSetController from Database.getQueryLocator over open Cases. In a large org the query matches 14,000 Cases, and the page fails with a LimitException. What explains it?
options: A set controller pages at most 500 records at a time, and calling setPageSize() above 500 throws a LimitException
Query locators are capped at 50,000 rows in Visualforce, and every row also counts toward the view state
Iteration components show 1,000 rows unless readOnly="true", and the overflow surfaces as a LimitException
The set controller handles 10,000 records; a query locator returning more throws, while a List is truncated
questions.explain: StandardSetController has a 10,000 record limit. Built from a query locator that returns more, it throws a LimitException; built from a list of more than 10,000 records, it silently truncates to the limit.
wrong: There is no 500-record page size limit; the problem is the total size of the set.
The 10,000 cap applies to the set controller regardless of the query locator's own limits, and the error is not about view state.
The 1,000-row iteration limit is real, but it raises a collection size error at render time, not this LimitException from the set controller.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: StandardSetController Class

questions.q: A security review flags the Visualforce page and controller below. Which risk did it find, and what is the fix?
questions.code:
<apex:page controller="CleanupController" action="{!removeContact}"/>

public with sharing class CleanupController {
    public PageReference removeContact() {
        Id cid = ApexPages.currentPage().getParameters().get('cid');
        delete [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE Id = :cid];
        return Page.CleanupDone;
    }
}
options: SOQL injection through the cid parameter; wrap it in String.escapeSingleQuotes() before using it in the query
CSRF: another site can send users here and the delete runs on load; delete only from a confirmed button click
XSS through cid; call HTMLENCODE on the parameter in the controller before using it in the query
Clickjacking: turn on clickjack protection for Visualforce pages, which stops the delete when the page is framed
questions.explain: The action attribute runs on page load, so the anti-CSRF token is never checked, and a link on any site can make a logged-in user delete records. Don't perform DML in a page action; require a user action such as a confirmation page with a button.
wrong: The parameter is a bind variable, which is already safe from SOQL injection.
HTMLENCODE is a Visualforce formula function for output, and the problem is the unprompted delete, not rendering.
Clickjack protection stops framing, but a plain link or redirect still runs the delete.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF); Secure Coding Guide

questions.q: Agents type notes with bold text and links in a rich text field. An LWC must show the formatted notes without opening an XSS hole. What should the developer use?
options: A div with lwc:dom="manual" whose innerHTML is set to the notes in renderedCallback()
<lightning-formatted-rich-text value={notes}>, which keeps allowed tags and strips the rest
A triple-brace binding such as {{{notes}}} in the template, so the HTML renders as markup
<lightning-formatted-text value={notes} linkify>, so that the HTML tags render as formatting
questions.explain: lightning-formatted-rich-text sanitizes the HTML it receives, keeping only allowed tags and attributes, which prevents XSS. Writing user data to innerHTML bypasses that protection.
wrong: innerHTML with user content is exactly how script injection happens.
LWC templates have no raw-HTML binding syntax.
lightning-formatted-text shows plain text and links; it doesn't render HTML formatting.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-formatted-rich-text
